ev.mng_fc_name.title: The name
ev.mng_fc_name.text: Your elders argue over what to call you. You could be given a "bad" name - Nergüi, "Nameless" - so that the evil spirits will pass by and not covet you. You could be named after the first thing seen at the threshold, as Yesügei named his son Temüjin after a captured Tatar. Or you could be named after your grandfather.
ev.mng_fc_name.protect.ok: They call you Nergüi, so the spirits will not know you. Only those closest to you know your real name.
ev.mng_fc_name.first_seen.ok: The first to ride up to the yurt is a messenger with news of a victory. It is a good omen - the name will be heard.
ev.mng_fc_name.grandfather.ok: Your grandfather takes you in his arms and murmurs his own name over you for a long time, as if handing on the whole camp with it.
ev.mng_fc_name.note: Mongols often gave children "repellent" names (Nergüi - "Nameless", Khünbish - "Not a person") to deceive evil spirits. According to the Secret History, Yesügei named his son Temüjin after the Tatar chief Temüjin-Üge whom he had captured.
ev.mng_fc_name_protect.text: You were badly ill in the spring but pulled through. Grandmother is pleased: the spirits looked for you by name - and could not find you.
ev.mng_fc_name_seen.text: The old courier you were named after rode by and gave you his whip: "Carry my name with honour."
ev.mng_fc_name_elder.text: Before he died your grandfather called you to him alone and recited the whole genealogy - nine generations back, to the forefather who came from Burkhan Khaldun.
ev.mng_fc_cord.title: The cord
ev.mng_fc_cord.text: The midwife has cut the cord with a sheep's bone and asks what to do with it. Some sew it into a little pouch and hang it on the cradle as a charm against illness. Others bury it under the hearth, so that the child will always come back to the home fire.
ev.mng_fc_cord.pouch: Sew it into a pouch for the cradle
ev.mng_fc_cord.pouch.ok: A patterned leather pouch dangles over the cradle. When you cry, they put it in your hands.
ev.mng_fc_cord.hearth.ok: A part of you now lies beneath the hearth. Wherever the yurt stands, its hearth is yours.
ev.mng_fc_cord.nothing.ok: The midwife shrugs and throws the cord into the fire.
ev.mng_fc_cord.note: Mongols and other steppe peoples had many birth rites: the cord and afterbirth were kept or buried to protect the child from evil forces and to "bind" it to its native place. Customs varied from clan to clan.
ev.mng_fc_cord_pouch.text: In winter half the camp went down with a cough, but the sickness passed you by. Grandmother touches the pouch at your neck meaningfully.
ev.mng_fc_cord_hearth.text: You come home after a long time away. You sit by the hearth - and suddenly understand that all that time this is exactly where you were being drawn.
ev.mng_fc_foal.title: Born the same day
ev.mng_fc_foal.text: On the same day as you, a foal was born in the herd and a white lamb in the flock. By custom a child is given its "age-mate" - an animal that will grow up alongside it. Which one will be chosen for you?
ev.mng_fc_foal.foal.ok: A mark is clipped into the foal's mane - your mark. He is yours from the very first day.
ev.mng_fc_foal.lamb.ok: A blue ribbon is tied round the white lamb's neck. He is the beginning of your herd.
ev.mng_fc_foal.note: Among Mongol herders a child was given livestock of its own from an early age; the animals grew up with it and became the core of its future household.
ev.mng_fc_foal_grown.text: Your age-mate foal has grown into a lively little horse, and now he will carry only you - anyone else he throws. You named him for his colour, and he comes to your whistle.
ev.mng_fc_lamb_herd.text: Your white lamb has already given rise to a little flock. You count it every evening and are as proud as a noyan.
ev.mng_fc_captive_mother.title: A lullaby in a foreign tongue
ev.mng_fc_captive_mother.text: You were born in your masters' yurt to a captive woman driven here from a distant land. She sings you a lullaby in her own tongue, though the mistress orders that the child be spoken to only in Mongol.
ev.mng_fc_captive_mother.her_tongue.ok: By day you hear Mongol speech, by night the soft words of her homeland.
ev.mng_fc_captive_mother.masters.ok: She falls silent and sings no more. You will speak like your masters.
ev.mng_fc_captive_mother.note: The Mongol campaigns drove tens of thousands of captives into the steppe - craftsmen, women and children. Their descendants often became Mongols, but memories of the homeland lived on in families for generations.
ev.mng_fc_tongue.text: At the bazaar you hear the speech of that lullaby - and answer in it. A merchant from the distant land laughs and gives you a handful of dried apples.
